          simple childhood innocence and conventional explanations of development that privilege sober and sensible adult outcomes. Instead, the play and lore of children is shown to be often
          disruptive, wayward, and irrational. The contributors variably con-sider and demonstrate "contextual" and "textual" ways of studying the folklore of children. Avoiding a narrow definition
          of the subject, they examine a variety of resources and approaches for studying, researching, and teaching it. These range from surveys of the history and literature of children's folklore
          to methods of field research, studies of genres of lore, and attempts to capture children's play and games.

title: Cecily Parsley's Nursery Rhymes
author: Beatrix Potter
description:
Cecily Parsley’s Nursery Rhymes is a children's book written and illustrated by Beatrix Potter, and published by Frederick Warne & Co. in December 1922. The book is a compilation
  of traditional nursery rhymes such as "Goosey Goosey Gander", "This Little Piggy" and "Three Blind Mice".

title: Cat & Dog Draw and Color
author: Elke Leisink, René Leisink
description: It's art time for Cat and Dog! What will they draw? What will YOU learn to draw?

title: Busy Ants
author: Kanchan Bannerjee
description: Follow the ants in this book. They are sure to keep young readers busy. This book is one of the four books in the 'Animals Around Us' series.

title: Botse-Botse Wants to Get Married
author: Ponlok Sidet
illustrator: Soeurm Kakada, Ven Che, So Chakrya, Yuom Kosal
description: After hearing wedding music in the village, Botse-Botse decides that she wants to get married too.

title: Bonda and Devi
author: Roopa Rai
description:
Do best friends always have to be alike? Devi and Bonda are best friends, but Devi is a little girl, while Bonda is a... Well, he can extend his arms and legs, and he never forgets
  anything he's told. Can you guess what is it?

title: Billo's Magic Journey (A Story From Kathmandu)
author: Rupy Singh
description:
With the success of her first book, "Rainbow Stories", Rupy Singh was encouraged to write this second book, "Billo's Magic Journey (A Story From Kathmandu)", which has definitely put
  her into the category of children's story writers.

title: Big blue bus
author: Mecelin Kakoro
description: Ebei and his mother are waiting for the big blue bus to take them to town. But the blue bus broke down. How will they get to town?

title: Bee's Sneeze
author: Pakaket Alford, Douglas J Alford
description: Billy wants to be a pollen picker but allergies are in the way. This is the story of overcoming obstacles to being the best that we can be.

title: Basim and Bloog
author: Unknown
description:
This story has been produced for UNESCO as part of its commitment to the FRESH initiative (Focussing Resources on Effective School Health). The story deal with issues such as
  hygiene, sanitation, disease prevention, violence, discrimination and disaster preparedness. Story telling and story writing can not only confirm knowledge and raise interest but also develop a
  whole range of language and life skills and enhance vital attitudes which children need to develop at school.

title: Around the World with a Chilli
author: Nayan Chanda
description:
Behind the humble chilli is a fascinating story that takes one around the world. This story is not just about the spicy chilli, but also about the adventures of brave warriors and
  traders, about stormy seas and new lands. Enjoy this fascinating account written by a renowned expert on globalization.

title: Annoying mosquito
author: Ursula Nafula
description: We all know the sound the mosquito makes as it buzzes in the night. Such a tiny insect but such a big pest!

title: Ann-Nem-Oh-Nee finds Adventure
author: Matthew Griffiths
description: Ann-Nem-Oh-Nee is stuck on her rock all alone. She’s looking for adventure and wants to see the world! But how?

title: Animals Run Away
author: Cissy Kiwanuka Luyiga
description: Four animals run away from their ungrateful owners to find a place to live on their own.

title: Angry Akku
author: Vinayak Varma
description: Akku is having an awful day and it’s making her very, VERY angry. Read this book to find out how Akku's anger melts away, and get ideas on what to do when YOU are very, VERY angry.

title: Anand
author: Rajiv Eipe
description: Meet Anand! He likes driving around and meeting new people. He likes music, dancing, and animals. He likes looking good, and he likes making your neighbourhood look good. He's awesome!

title: An unexpected adventure
author: Carina Jooste
description: A boring afternoon turns into an exciting adventure when a little boy opens a book.

title: Ammu and the Sparrows
author: Vinitha R
description: Ammu spends his days with Ammamma. He feeds the birds and waits to see if Amma and Accha sparrow will come visit.

title: Africa Unity Race
author: Nina Orange
description: The story is about two young people who run across Africa to spread the message of unity. On the way, others join the race.

title: Adventures in Toyland
author: Edith King Hall
description: British writer of children's books; later became Edith King Hall; the daughter of Charles King Hall (1845-1895), professor of music. Elocutionist (1901)

title: Activate Games for Learning American English – Picture This
author: American English
keywords: Activate Games for Learning American English
description:
Activate: Games for Learning American English is a collection of games for the language classroom. The games in Activate offer interactive English language practice in a
  learner-centered, low-stress environment. Picture This cards are a set of cards that can be used for a variety of conversation and word games in English classes.

title: Aaloo-Maaloo-Kaaloo
author: Vinita Krishna
description:
One day Maaloo had to get some potatoes from his kitchen garden. Who do you think helped him? Kaaloo, of course! Read about Maaloo's morning with Kaaloo as they found some
  'Aaloo'!

title: A Very Green Day
author: Phạm Thu Thùy
description: Greeny has so much energy. She doesn't want to nap! One day, she decides to run away. After playing in the hot sun for a while, Greeny gets tired and wants to go home. But now she's lost! How will she get home to her dad?

title: A Tiny Seed
author: Nicola Rijsdijk
description:
In a village on the slopes of Mount Kenya, a little girl worked in the fields with her mother. She worried as she saw the big forests disappearing, but she knew the power of a tiny
  seed.

title: A Special Nest
author: Kavita Singh
description: A bird is trying to build a nest for herself. But everywhere she builds a nest, something or the other disturbs her. What will she do?

title: A Scary Pit
author: Chanchal Sharma
description: Samira loves to cycle! But suddenly she stops when she hears a goat bleating…

title: A Record Year for Rainfall
author: Dave Marquesen
description: A sketchbook made into a story featuring some nice items for geography and science lessons while reading.

title: A Popular Schoolgirl
author: Angela Brazil
description: Ingred and her family must move from Rotherwood, their stately home, to a smaller Bungalow when their post-Great War finances take a turn for the worse. The story follows Ingred's year at school - now a boarder - where she is made form 'warden', and has to contend with new girl Bess who has moved into her former home.

title: A New View
author: Phal Tithlyhong
description: Tulu wants to be a photographer just like his father. But it's harder than he'd expected! Can Tulu learn to take great photographs at the festival?

title: A Little Princess
author: Frances Hodgson Burnett
description:
Seven-year-old Sara Crewe is sent to live at Miss Minchin's boarding school in London. Her father, Captain Crewe, is a doting young man who leaves instructions that his
          daughter is to be given a private room with a parlor, a maid, and anything else she might desire in his absence.

title: A Little Monkey and a Fish
author: Nguon Sakal
description: A Little Monkey and a Fish is a story about a young, playful, and clever monkey who learns to make his way in the world by mimicking his mother. Along his journey, he must decide whether or not to take some risks. What do you think he will do?

title: A Leaf Goes on a Trip
author: Anagha Kusum
keywords: A Leaf Goes on a Trip
description: A leaf flew in the wind. It went far and wide. In the end, it landed in Kabeer’s home. What did Kabeer do with the leaf?

title: A Fair to Remember
author: Bharati Jagannathan
description:
Set in sixteen century Vijayanagara, this is a story about three friends who meet a stranger in a fair. It showcases the history, grandeur, colour and drama of the times, making the
  reader want to gallop on an Arabian horse into the exciting kingdom of the great Krishnadevaraya himself.

title: A Double Story
author: George Macdonald
publisher: Penn State Electronic Classic Series Publication
description:
Also known as "A Double Story" or "The Wise Woman", the story of two very spoiled girls, a princess and a peasant, who are kidnapped by a strange woman for a lesson in life.
          They may not emerge the same... but will their parents be changed for the better too?

title: A Butterfly Smile
author: Mathangi Subramanian
description: Kavya’s family has just moved from her village to Bengaluru and she is the newest girl in her class. Go along with Kavya as she visits a butterfly park where she discovers a special connection with butterflies and also makes a new friend.

title: लौ भन त म के गर्दैछु !
author: Unknown
description:
यो पुस्तकको अंग्रेजी संस्करणमा विश्वका विभिन्न क्षेत्रको प्रतिनिधित्व हुने गरी सात वटा गाउँ र शहरसँग सम्बन्धित कथा राखिएका थिए। यो नेपाली संस्करणमा नेपालको एक सचित्र कथा पनि सम्मिलित
  गराइएको छ।

title: Zzzizi Drinks Blood
author: Child-to-Child Trust
description:
This story has been produced for UNESCO as part of its commitment to the FRESH initiative (Focussing Resources on Effective School Health). The story deal with issues such as
  hygiene, sanitation, disease prevention, violence, discrimination and disaster preparedness. Story telling and story writing can not only confirm knowledge and raise interest but also develop a
  whole range of language and life skills and enhance vital attitudes which children need to develop at school.

title: Zogs and Cogs: A Tale of Teamwork
author: Pakaket Alford, Douglas J Alford
description:
Two groups of people struggle to survive. At the start, the Ogs hunt mammoths. The Zogs each pick their own food from plants. This is a story of learning to work together in teams.
  Words on cogs offer advise. Together the Zogs go from famine to feast. Food and freezing changes lead to a surprise finish.

title: Zogs 2 – More Teams
author: Pakaket Alford, Douglas J Alford
description:
Ancestor Zogs had success going from famine to feast. They were full. Overtime, the Zogs forgot the useful cog words. Today, the Zogs are hungry again. This is the story about
  relearning lost lessons. The Zogs rediscover the power of teamwork to fix long-term problems. So can we!

title: Zibu and Zizo
author: Refilwe Nsibande
description: Zibu and Zizo are twin brothers. They are similar, but different. Being different is not bad, it’s great.

title: Zandi and Birdy Monster
author: Marie-Louise Rouget
description: Zandi has a friend that no one else can see. His name is Birdy Monster. They mix up magic potions, play pretend and go on adventures together.

title: You Won't Believe Me
author: Jairaj Singh
keywords: I Know You Won't Believe Me
description: Here is a boy who likes his school a lot, but is sure that his school does not like him back. His classmates bully him. His teachers shout at him. But there is a pond full of fish — where he discovers that he’s not alone.

title: You Don't Understand
author: Julieana Philip
description: Selvi demands that her family do everything her way. But does Selvi really know best? Find out how Selvi learns about respect.

title: Yapo Saves The Day
author: Rujeko Moyo
description: Yapo loves to play soccer! But he does not like to pass the ball to his teammates. How will Yapo discover that winning is not only about scoring?

title: Wolfie
author: Janet Chenery
description:
Wolfie is the pet spider of George and Harry. Polly, Harry’s sister helps in feeding the spider though the boys try their best to keep her out of their way. The story interestingly
  depicts the children’s fascination for their pet and their natural curiosity to know more about it.

title: Willis The Pilot: A Sequel To The Swiss Family Robinson
author: Johann David Wyss, Adrien Paul

title: Wildlife in a City Pond
author: Ashish Kothari
description:
Wetlands in any city are seen mostly a wasteland, waiting to be built over. It takes a tireless environmentalist to show us what city pounds really are - magically rich ecosystems
  worth preserving. Based on a real-life experience, here is a story that introduces us to the delightful fauna and flora in the urban landscape.

title: Wild Cat! Wild Cat!
author: Sejal Mehta
description: Meet the different wild cats of India.

title: Wikijunior Languages
author: Wikibooks Contributors
description:
Some languages do not have any tenses. This means that there is only one way to say a verb. Imagine saying I go to school yesterday. In these languages, words like yesterday
          and tomorrow are used to say when you did something. Other languages even use pictures! Learn about various languages of the world.

title: Wiggle Jiggle
author: Mathapelo Mabaso
description: Wiggle jiggle wriggle with the wiggly worm, on a fun adventure that is full of surprises.

title: Why, Oh Why!
author: Richa Bhaskar
description: Here is a book that will make little readers make faces at each other!

title: Why does a Poori Puff Up?
author: Varsha Joshi
description: Round, fat pooris are a treat in most Indian homes. Why do they puff up? There is a whole lot of science behind this simple question.

title: Why Hippos Have No Hair
author: David Ker, Basilio Gimo
description:
Hares are popular creatures in African folktales. They are famous for behaving badly and always getting away with it. In this Nyungwe folktale, we see what happens when Hare refuses
  to forgive Hippo for stepping on his foot. - See more at: http://www.africanstorybook.org/stories/why-hippos-have-no-hair#sthash.tUh6458B.dpuf

title: Why Do Bees Buzz?
author: Nabanita Deshmukh
description: Why can't bees work quietly? They buzz because there are some very good reasons to do so. Learn about the humble bees in this book.

title: Why Can’t We Glow Like Fireflies?
author: Unknown
keywords: Why can't we glow like Fireflies?
description: Did you know that fireflies are also called lightning bugs? And did you know that baby fireflies use their glow to chase away predators? Jump right into this book if you want to find out more about these creatures that light up the dark.

title: Why Can't We Glow Like Fireflies?
author: Nabanita Deshmukh
description:
Did you know that fireflies are also called lightning bugs? And did you know that baby fireflies use their glow to chase away predators? Find out more about these creatures that
  light up the dark.

title: Whose button is this?
author: Louise Gale, Paul Kennedy, James Woolley
description: Tinny Tim sets out on an adventure to return a lost button. Along the way he goes exploring, has a miraculous escape, and makes new friends.

title: Whoop, Goes The PufferFish
author: Sejal Mehta
description: A baby Pufferfish is stuck in a shallow pool of seawater. Will it find its way back home to the sea?

title: Who's that Baby?
author: Chisanga Mukuka
description: A new baby has come to play. Who could it be?

title: Who is it?
author: Kanchan Bannerjee
description: Srr.. Srr.. Who do you think is making this sound? Priya will find out in this story!

title: Who is Big?
author: Sara Saunders
description: Ant looks around him and sees that he is big compared to the objects around him. But is Ant really big? Who is really big?

title: Who Took My Shoe?
author: Elana Bregin
description: Jabulani has lost his school shoe. He can’t find it anywhere. Where can it be?

title: Who Did What In World History?
author: Pakaket Alford, Douglas J Alford
keywords: Who Did What In World History
description:
Practice your English with "Who Did What In World History." This is the interesting story about people from our past. What they did echoes in our modern life. Knowing who they were
  helps us know where we fit on this one world.

title: Who Ate the Pink Sweetmeat?
author: Susan Coolidge
description: A collection of classic and cherished Christmas stories enjoyed by generations. The stories include: Who Ate The Pink Sweetmeat? by Susan Coolidge, The Whizzer by Mary Hartwell Catherwood, The Patroncito's Christmas by F. L. Stealey, Cherry Pie by Kate Upson Clark, Bertie's Ride by Lady Dunboyne, and Asaph Sheafe's Christmas by E. E. Hale.

title: Who Am I?
author: Unknown
description: An animal who has a pocket on its stomach and can jump really far! Can you guess its name?

title: Where is the Moon?
author: Kanchan Bannerjee
description: Where does the moon go during the day? Come, let’s find out.

title: Where is My Bat?
author: Meera Tendolkar
description: Now and then you hear a child talking to himself and describing an event. And how vivid the sketch is! 'Where is My Bat?' is one such lively account.

title: Where is Gogo?
author: Mala Kumar, Manisha Chaudhry
description: When Toto spotted Gogo's empty cage, he knew he was in trouble. Would you like to help Toto find Gogo?

title: Where Do Cookies Come From?
author: Pakaket Alford, Douglas J Alford
description:
We like to eat them, but just where do chocolate chip cookies come from? This book shows you how the parts come together to make the whole cookie. Now that is one smart - about to be
  eaten - cookie.

title: Where Did Your Dimples Go?
author: Radha HS
description:
Langlen has curly hair like Appa and a cleft chin like Imma. It makes her wonder why brothers and sisters, or parents and children look alike. Is she just a collection of traits
  then? So many questions, but Imma and Appa have all the answers.

title: When I Grow Up
author: Simóne van der Spuy, Michele Fry, Jennifer Jacobs
description: I don’t know what I want to be when I grow up. Can you help me choose?

title: What's in the Lunch Box?
author: Somesuntharam Shanmugapriya
description: Mithusan's keeps staring at his lunch box all day. But there's no food in there, so why can't he take his eyes off of it? Find out what’s in the box and the power of being compassionate.

title: What's That Smell?
author: Ashwitha Jayakumar
description: Someone’s been eating all of Madhav and Tara’s food. Strange creatures, fuzzy monsters, or something invisible? Who could it be?

title: What's Next?
author: Rayhaanah Williams
description: Once the school bell rings, the excitement begins. Grandpa picks Fatima up from school. What adventures will they have?

title: What shall I wear today?
author: Natasha Sharma
description: On some days, it is so difficult to decide what to wear. The little girl in this story tries on many dresses before she finds the perfect one.

title: What shall I use to travel?
author: Ursula Nafula
keywords: What shall I use to travel?
description: Child thinks of travelling and wonders what is the best means of transport.

title: What a song !
author: Jitendra Thakur
description: What a song ! a bundelkhandi folk tale

title: What a Nasty Hero [A Collection of Child Stories]
author: Kartikeya Ghimire

title: What If?
author: Hari Kumar Nair
description: When Shyam is sleepy he has trouble brushing his teeth. But dreaming big is no trouble at all.

title: Wet Magic
author: Edith Nesbit
description:
When four siblings journey to the seashore for a holiday, one of them unwittingly summons the sister of a mermaid who is captured by a circus, and the children set out to
          save the imprisoned being. After a daring midnight rescue, the children's reward is an incredible journey beneath the waves and into the hidden kingdom of the mermaids. But they soon find
          themselves in a race against time as they struggle to prevent a war and save their new underwater companions...

title: Weather book
author: Zanele Buthelezi, Clare Verbeek, Thembani Dladla
description: Explore different types of weather and how we feel about the weather.

title: We are Friends
author: Gunani Sirisena
description: Little Rabbit doesn't tolerate anyone who is different from her and she doesn't try to make friends. But what happens when she needs help crossing a dangerous creek?

title: We Are All Animals
author: Meera Tendolkar, Madhav Chavan
description: Big ideas in fun stories for children to read and enjoy.

title: Water Dance
author: Sean D'mello
description: Guddu can dance to anything. Today he has found music in water and can’t stop doing a jig as he makes his way down a stream. A story that introduces water bodies and celebrates the joy of water.

title: Watch Out! The Tiger is Here!
author: Sejal Mehta
description: When a tiger moves through the forest, all the animals and birds know! Listen to the different alarm calls that warn everyone in the forest that the tiger is here.

title: Wally the Worm
author: Unknown
description:
This story has been produced for UNESCO as part of its commitment to the FRESH initiative (Focussing Resources on Effective School Health). The story deal with issues such as
  hygiene, sanitation, disease prevention, violence, discrimination and disaster preparedness. Story telling and story writing can not only confirm knowledge and raise interest but also develop a
  whole range of language and life skills and enhance vital attitudes which children need to develop at school.

title: Veeru Goes to the Circus
author: Richa Ingle Deo
description: Veeru comes back from the Jumbo-Mumbo Circus with some very big ideas. Read on to find out more.

title: Vayu, the Wind
author: Madhuri Pai
description: Big ideas in fun stories for children to read and enjoy.

title: Unwise judge
author: Elizabeth Laird, Brian Wambi, Magabi Eynew Gessesse
description:
Two men twice accept the advice of a bad judge. It is only when they eventually consult the elders, who listen carefully to their story, that the men can restore their friendship.
  (This story was originally narrated by Magabi Eynew Gessesse. The English version was written by Elizabeth Laird.)

title: Uncle Wiggily's Adventure Part II
author: Howard R. Garis
description: Uncle Wiggily, an engaging elderly rabbit, is lame from rheumatism. Whenever he goes anywhere, he always relies on what Garis describes as "his candy-striped walking cane" - this is a cane striped red and white like a peppermint candy cane.

title: Uncle Wiggily's Adventure Part I
author: Howard R. Garis
description: Uncle Wiggily, an engaging elderly rabbit, is lame from rheumatism. Whenever he goes anywhere, he always relies on what Garis describes as "his candy-striped walking cane" - this is a cane striped red and white like a peppermint candy cane.

title: Uncle Wiggily and Mother Goose Part I
author: Howard R. Garis
description: Beginning in 1910, Howard Roger Garis penned an Uncle Wiggily tale every day (except Sundays) for 30 years, much to the delight of both children and adult fans of the elderly gentleman rabbit. Join Uncle Wiggily in outwitting such outrageous creatures as the Pipsiseweh, Skeeziks, Bazumpus, Crozokus and the Scuttlemagoon while teaching heartwarming life lessons.

title: Uncle George feeds his Baby
author: Unknown
description:
This story has been produced for UNESCO as part of its commitment to the FRESH initiative (Focussing Resources on Effective School Health). The story deal with issues such as
  hygiene, sanitation, disease prevention, violence, discrimination and disaster preparedness. Story telling and story writing can not only confirm knowledge and raise interest but also develop a
  whole range of language and life skills and enhance vital attitudes which children need to develop at school.

title: Unathi and the Dirty, Smelly Beast
author: Jon Keevy
description: Something is following Unathi…

title: Two
author: Carole Bloch
description: Simple sentences about things in pairs or twos - hands, feet, ears, eyes and arms.

title: Twilight Land
author: Howard Pyle
description:
It is evening at the Inn of the Sign of Mother Goose. In a dark, smoky room, the world’s most famous storytellers gather to weave tales of mystery and
  enchantment.(Goodreads)

title: Turtle Trouble
author: Agnes de Bezenac, Salem
description:
Telling the truth, or covering up? That’s what our little character in this story is mulling over in his little mind. A short story told from a child's perspective, aimed at teaching
  children hows and whys of good behaviour.

title: Turtle Jumps! A Tale of Determination
author: Pakaket Alford, Douglas J Alford
description: A Turtle named TJ wants to jump. How can a turtle jump? This story teaches us all how to keep trying until we succeed.

title: Turtle Dove
author: Komar Rien Komar Cheh
description: Learn what Turtle Dove can and cannot do!

title: Tumi Goes to the Park
author: Paballo Rampa
description: It’s Tumi’s first visit to the park. She’s so excited, there are many adventures. She might even make a new friend.

title: Tree Trips - Wide Wonderful World
author: Pakaket Alford, Douglas J Alford
description: A tree goes on a trip. It helps make the city a better place to live in. The tree learns that the world is a wide and wonderful place.

title: Travelling across dinner-tables
author: Alexandra Grigorieva
description: This publication was prepared by the Charity Foundation Institute of Tolerance (Russia) with the help of the UNESCO Moscow Office.

title: Tottochan: The Little Girl at the Window
author: Tetsuko Kuroyanagi, Dorothy Britton

title: Tortoise Finds His Home
author: Maya Fowler, Katrien Coetzer, Damian Gibbs
description: Tortoise is looking for its house. Other animals help Tortoise look. Will they find Tortoise's house together?

title: Tortoise Finds His Home
author: Damian Gibbs
description:
Tortoise sets off in search of his house. Along the way, he meets new friends to help him. But the sky is darkening, and lightning flashes in the distance. Will Tortoise find his
  house in time?

title: Too small
author: Media Matters
description: Lebo has grown out of all her clothes and they are now too small for her. What will she do with them?

title: Too Much TV: Undo Too-Tain-Itis
author: Pakaket Alford, Douglas J Alford
description:
Ta spends most of his time in front of the TV. One day Ta doesn’t feel well. The Doctor tells Ta, “You have Too-Tain-Itis.” This story teaches us how to undo too much
  TV.

title: Too Many Bananas
author: Noni
description: No one wanted to buy the sweet bananas that Sringeri Srinivas grew on his farm. Find out what he did with them in this cute story.

title: Tone's Big Drop
author: Edna Gicovi
description: Tone the raindrop is wondering what’s way down there on the ground. She and her friend Nyunyu go on a journey to find out.

title: Ting Tong
author: Lubaina Bandukwala
description: How can the baby sleep with so many sounds around him? Find out what disturbs our little one.

title: Tine and the Faraway Mountain
author: Shikha Tripathi
description: Whooshoo! Whooshoo! In the hilly town of Echali, Tine hears a whisper. It's the mountains calling to her. As she grows up, Tine dreams of getting closer to her beloved mountains. But can she reach the top of the highest mountain in the world? Based on the life of a mountaineer from Arunachal Pradesh, this book celebrates the power of dreams and believing in yourself.

title: Timmy and Pepe
author: Madhav Chavan, Flavia Ribeiro de Castro
description: Harvest time is here and it begins with Reireidaar’s big day. Will she cut the first sheaf of the harvest or will her imagination get in the way?

title: Timmy and Pepe
author: Manisha Vengurlekar, Madhav Chavan
description: Come, listen to Timmy and Pepe talk to each other. Do you also like to talk to your pet?

title: Tikky! Boom! Tish!
author: Sam Wilson
description: Everyone can make music! Just say: Boom! Tikky! Wubba! Tish!

title: Tiger, Tiger, Where Are You?
author: Mujahid Khan
keywords: Tiger, Tiger, Where Are You?Tiger, Tiger, Where Are You?
description: A tiger researcher is out looking for tiger hair and poop as part of his study. He finds plenty of signs of the tiger, but where is the big cat? After all, there are so many ways to see a tiger without seeing a tiger.

title: Tibetan-English Folktales
author: Tshe dbang rdo rje, dPal Idan bKra shis, Kevin Stuart, Allie Thomas, 'Gyur med rgya mtsho
description:
The folktales in this book were collected by students in the 1997 and the 1998 English Teaching Training classes studying in the, at that time, Nationalities Department,
          Qinghai Normal University during summer and winter holidays. Allie Thomas and Kevin Stuart edited the English translations of the versions given to us by the students, which were then
          translated back into Tibetan by the students and edited by Tse dbang rdo rje, dPal ldan bkra shis and 'Gyur med rgya mtsho. Students who use this book should first try to understand the
          stories without looking at the Tibetan translations. Because most answers to the exercises can be found by reading the texts, students should not look at either the Tibetan or English
          versions until they have finished the exercises.

title: Thunder and Lightning
author: Owino Ogot, Athieno Gertrude
description: Thunder and her son, Lightning, lived on earth amongst people. Due to her destructive, naughty son the king sent them to live in the sky away from people.

title: Through The Looking Glass
author: Lewis Carroll
description: Six months after her visit to wonderland Alice, falls through her glass mirror and enters a fantastical world of life size chess pieces and nursery rhyme characters.

title: Three-P, the fifth musketeer
author: Nick Creech
description:
The adventures of Three-P, an unsuspecting fairy penguin adventurer, musketeer, and hero. Three-P fights peer pressure and prejudice, but follows his heart and in doing so learns the
  value of friendship, and how to be a real hero.

title: They are not little Fish
author: Novia Erwida
description: The dish Mother cooked is very delicious. Fitri thinks it’s crispy flakes, but in fact it’s not. It’s made out of tiny fish. If the little ones are so good, why the bigger ones are not?

title: The top button
author: Konstantina Charlavani, Maria Chatzi
description:
Brighty is a cute and brilliant button, which wants people to know how outstanding he is. Everyone does admire him until the day he is forced to share the attention with his
          relatives, who are none other than buttons that look exactly like him. His life completely changes and led by disappointment and frustration he lives an adventure which teaches him what it
          means to be truly remarkable.

title: The sun who lost his way
author: Evridiki Amanatidou
keywords: The sun who lost his way
description:
“And what is so wrong with my liking game playing instead of learning Geography?”. That’s what the naughty sun, Shiny, kept saying all the time. Anyway, the time he should rise and
  shine in order to start a new day for people has come. And then… Then, things got a bit tougher. Cheerful and eager, he began, but soon he got confused and lost his way. What should people do to
  help the naughty little one? A story about the importance of everything, no matter small or big, and the power of helping each other.

title: The sprouting bean
author: Zanele Buthelezi, Clare Verbeek, Thembani Dladla
description: Plant a bean seed and see what happens when you water and look after it.

title: The jealousy germ
author: Μaria Chatzi, Ioanna Teknetzi
description:
In a small but famous bakery, they all work together, respecting and loving each other. One day the terrible Jealousy germ sneaks in. From that day on, life in the bakery changes.
  How does the germ manage to become the master of the place? And how will they get rid of it? This is a story about a germ that’s different from all other germs, and which could sneak into your
  house or your classroom as well. Read this book and you will, no doubt, be ready to deal with it.

title: The fairytale of the Heart of a Monkey
author: Andrew Lang
description: The fairytale of the Heart of a Monkey retold by Andrew Lang

title: The fairytale of Hansel and Gretel
author: Brothers Grimm
description: The classic fairy tale that celebrates Hansel and Gretel's strength and spirit over the malevolence of the world around them.

title: The coffee legend
author: Alemu Abebe, CODE Ethiopia
description: Tells about the origin of coffee in Ethiopia.

title: The boy, the girl and the very tiny reality
author: Stefany Veldemiry, Eva Smirli-Bainbridge
keywords: The boy, the girl and the very tiny reality
description:
Within a seashell was hiding one very tiny reality. There lived a mermaid girl. One day, a handsome boy saw her and said to her “Hey, little girl! As soon as I finish eating
          my fish, I will come to kiss you.” Their love was so deep, it was deeper than the deepest sea…

title: The Youngest Girl in the Fifth
author: Angela Brazil
description: The book explores how the well-meaning intention of teachers having kids jump one class makes it emotionally challenging for them to adjust. The same story is written here although the girl is really brilliant and smart she finds difficulty in adjusting to the hatred of her classmates. Now let’s not spoil the complete story for you, but it was a time where the stories were supposed to be all about teaching moral science lessons, so you can expect the end.

title: The Windy Hill
author: Cornelia Meigs
description: A family mystery is unraveled by a boy and girl visiting their uncle one summer. The story combines history and modern plot in a stirring way.

title: The Wind In The Willows
author: Kenneth Grahame
description: The Wind In The Willows is a timeless tale of animal cunning and human camaraderie.

title: The Water Babies: A Fairy Tale For A Land Baby
author: Charles Kingsley
description:
The protagonist is Tom, a young chimney sweep, who falls into a river after encountering an upper-class girl named Ellie and being chased out of her house. There he dies and
          is transformed into a "water baby", as he is told by a caddis fly—an insect that sheds its skin—and begins his moral education. The story is thematically concerned with Christian
          redemption, though Kingsley also uses the book to argue that England treats its poor badly, and to question child labour, among other themes.

title: The Voyages of Doctor Dolittle
author: Hugh Lofting
description:
The Voyages of Doctor Dolittle was the second of Hugh Lofting's Doctor Dolittle books to be published, coming out in 1922. It is nearly four times longer than its predecessor
          and the writing style is pitched at a more mature audience. The scope of the novel is vast; it is divided into six parts and the illustrations are also more sophisticated. It won the
          Newbery Medal for 1923. [wikipedia]

title: The Velveteen Rabbit
author: Margery Williams
description:
Nursery magic is very strange and wonderful, and only those playthings that are old and wise and experienced like the Skin Horse understand all about it. Like the Skin Horse, Margery
  Williams understood how toys--and people--become real through the wisdom and experience of love. This reissue of a favorite classic, with the original story and illustrations as they first appeared
  in 1922, will work its magic for all who read it.

title: The Ugly Princess
author: Janaki Sooriyarachchi
description:
A king and his queen have everything they could want in life except children. A magician grants them their wish of a child but on the condition that they only do good deeds. However,
  an unkind act to a poor urchin leads the magician to place a curse on the couple causing their daughter to be born extremely ugly. The girl grows up very saddened by her appearance. Her life is
  full of unhappiness until one day she discovers a prince who has also been the victim of a bad spell.

title: The Timid Train
author: Bharati Jagannathan
description:
Loco, the new train felt rather scared of going anywhere. But every time is let out an 'Ooo!' in fright, it came out as a strong whistle and everybody said Loco was a fine train.
  Come take a ride with Loco as it chugs merrily across the country.

title: The Tiffin Gang
author: Shweta Ganesh Kumar
description: Meenu dislikes tiffin time because Amma always gives her idlis. But what do her classmates bring for lunch? Meenu decides to peek into their boxes and find out.

title: The Three Little Kittens
author: Chou Chinith
description: Three little kittens are afraid of the neighbourhood dog. He really wants to play with them, but whenever they see him they run away! Why do you think they are so scared of him?

title: The Tales of Mother Goose
author: Charles Perrault
description:
Beloved fairy tale author Charles Perrault published the first known version of The Tales of Mother Goose in 1697, under the French title Histoires ou contes du temps passés,
          avec des moralités. The collection includes "The Sleeping Beauty", "Little Red Riding Hood", and "Cinderella", as well as many others that would go on to become adored favourites, several
          of which are thought to be inventions of Perrault himself.

title: The Tale of the Pie and the Patty-Pan
author: Beatrix Potter
description:
Potter declared the tale her next favourite to The Tailor of Gloucester, but the tale is not popular among modern children, perhaps because they have difficulty following the
  complications involving the pies and because they have no experience with old-fashioned ovens and fireplaces. The pictures however are some of the most beautiful Potter ever created, especially the
  profusions of flowers in the doorways and garden plots.

title: The Tale of the Juniper Tree
author: Brothers Grimm
description:
A boy is killed by his stepmother. In an attempt to cover up the murder, the woman bakes the boy into a pudding and feeds the boy to his father. The boy's sister collects his
          bones, and as she cries over them they become a bird which flies away. The bird kills the stepmother by dropping a millstone on her. The bird is turned back into a boy and he, his sister,
          and his father live together happily.

title: The Tale of Tom Kitten
author: Beatrix Potter
description:
The tale begins with three feline siblings – Mittens, Tom Kitten, and Moppet – tumbling about the doorstep and playing in the dust. Their mother, Mrs. Tabitha Twitchit,
          expects "fine company" for tea so she fetches the children indoors to wash and dress them before her friends arrive.

title: The Tale of Timmy Tiptoes
author: Beatrix Potter
description:
The tale is set in a forest and begins with "once upon a time". Timmy Tiptoes is "a little fat comfortable grey squirrel" living in a nest thatched with leaves in the top of a tall
  tree with his little wife, Goody. Over the course of several days, the two collect nuts in their little sacks for the coming winter and spring, and store the nuts in hollow tree stumps near their
  home. Timmy wears a red jacket he removes while working, and his wife wears a pink dress and apron. [wikipedia]

title: The Tale of Squirrel Nutkin
author: Beatrix Potter
description:
Squirrel Nutkin, his brother Twinkleberry, and their many cousins sail to Owl Island on little rafts they have constructed of twigs. They offer resident owl Old Brown a gift and ask
  his permission to do their nut-collecting on his island. [wikipedia]

title: The Tale of Mrs. Tittlemouse
author: Beatrix Potter
description:
Mrs. Tittlemouse is a "most terribly tidy little mouse always sweeping and dusting the soft sandy floors" in the "yards and yards" of passages and storerooms, nut-cellars,
          and seed-cellars in her "funny house" amongst the roots of a hedge. [wikipedia]

title: The Tale of Mrs. Tiggy-Winkle
author: Beatrix Potter
description:
A little girl named Lucie lives on a farm called Little-town. She is a good little girl, but has lost three handkerchiefs and a pinafore. She questions Tabby Kitten and Sally
          Henny-penny about them, but they know nothing.

title: The Tale of Mr. Jeremy Fisher
author: Beatrix Potter
keywords: The Tale of Mr. Jeremy Fisher
description:
Jeremy Fisher is a frog who lives in a "slippy-sloppy" house at the edge of a pond. One rainy day he collects worms for fishing, and sets off across the pond on his lily-pad
          boat.

title: The Tale of Johnny Town-Mouse
author: Beatrix Potter
description:
Timmy Willie is a country mouse who falls asleep in a hamper of vegetables and is carried to the city. When the hamper is opened, Timmy escapes to find himself in a large house. He
  slips through a hole in the skirting board and lands in the midst of a mouse dinner party hosted by Johnny Town-mouse.

title: The Tale of Jemima Puddle-Duck
author: Beatrix Potter
description:
The tale begins in a farmyard which is home to a duck called Jemima Puddle-duck. She wants to hatch her own eggs, but the farmer's wife believes ducks make poor sitters and routinely
  confiscates their eggs to allow the hens to incubate them. Jemima tries to hide her eggs, but they are always found and carried away. She sets off along the road in poke bonnet and shawl to find a
  safe place away from the farm to lay her eggs. [wikipedia]

title: The Tale Of Piper
author: Ana P. Dewiyanav
description: In the garden, a little girl plays a sad song on her flute. Why is she so sad? Maybe the inhabitants of the garden can help!

title: The Tale Of Peter Rabbit: Fill in the dots
author: Beatrix Potter

title: The Tailor of Gloucester
author: Beatrix Potter
description:
A tailor in Gloucester sends his cat Simpkin to buy food and a twist of cherry-coloured silk to complete a waistcoat commissioned by the mayor for his wedding on Christmas
          morning. While Simpkin is gone, the tailor finds mice the cat has imprisoned under teacups. The mice are released and scamper away. When Simpkin returns and finds his mice gone, he hides
          the twist in anger. [wikipedia]

title: The Swiss Family Robinson
author: Johann David Wyss
description:
The Swiss Family Robinson (German: Der Schweizerische Robinson) is a novel, first published in 1812, about a Swiss family who are shipwrecked in the East Indies en route to Port
  Jackson, Australia.

title: The Sunshower Song
author: Vinayak Varma
description: When the sun shines on a rainy day, all the animals of the forest know what’s about to happen: music and magic at the jackals’ wedding! The wedding guests each bring a scrap of sound. Some bring rhythm, and some bring tune, in this lyrical ode to the popular sunshower legend.

title: The Story of a Piece of Paper
author: Katya Jubb, Natalie Jubb
keywords: The Story of a Piece of Paper
description:
A blank piece of paper and a child’s imagination is all you need for an adventure. What can you do with a blank piece of paper? Draw a picture – it might come to life. Make an
  envelope – something unexpected may be hiding inside. Write a story – it might escape off the page into the world.

title: The Story of Miss Moppet
author: Beatrix Potter
description: The tale begins with an illustration of a wide-eyed kitten: "This is a Pussy called Miss Moppet, she thinks she has heard a mouse!"

title: The Story of Doctor Dolittle
author: Hugh Lofting
description:
Join Doctor Dolittle on his grandest adventures. Join the good doctor as he leans to talk with the animals, squeak and squawk with the animals. Read along as he meets the
          pushmi-pullyu, The Purple Bird-of-paradise, and many many others.

title: The Story Of Mankind
author: Hendrik Willem van Loon
description:
The Story of Mankind was written and illustrated by American journalist, professor, and author Hendrik Willem van Loon and published in 1921. In 1922, it was the first book
          to be awarded the Newbery Medal for an outstanding contribution to children's literature.

title: The Special Panter
author: Dương Ngọc Tú Quỳnh
description: Teo is missing the fingers on his right hand, but he loves painting and hopes to become a painter. Do you think Teo will be able to live out his dream in art class?

title: The Song Competition
author: Unknown
description:
This story has been produced for UNESCO as part of its commitment to the FRESH initiative (Focussing Resources on Effective School Health). The story deal with issues such as
  hygiene, sanitation, disease prevention, violence, discrimination and disaster preparedness. Story telling and story writing can not only confirm knowledge and raise interest but also develop a
  whole range of language and life skills and enhance vital attitudes which children need to develop at school.

title: The Snail's Wonderful Journey
author: Aruna Keerthi Gamage
description: Cheta the Snail wants to take a bus journey. He tries many times to catch the bus, but it is not as easy as he hoped! Will his dream ever come true?

title: The Secrets of Rocks
author: Suchi Govindarajan
description: Rocks are everywhere — under the ground, above the ground, and even at the bottom of our oceans. But where do rocks come from? What are they made of? If rocks could talk, they would share many secrets.

title: The Sea Fairies
author: Lyman Frank Baum
description:
Mayre Griffiths, nicknamed Trot, or sometimes Tiny Trot, is a little girl who lives on the coast of southern California. Her father is the captain of a sailing schooner, and her
  constant companion is Cap'n Bill Weedles, a retired sailor with a wooden leg. (Cap'n Bill had been Trot's father's skipper, and Charlie Griffiths had been his mate, before the accident that took
  the older man's leg.) Trot and Cap'n Bill spend many of their days roaming the beaches near home, or rowing and sailing along the coast. One day, Trot wishes that she could see a mermaid; her wish
  is overheard, and granted the next day. The mermaids explain to Trot, and the distressed Cap'n Bill, that they are benevolent fairies; when they offer Trot a chance to pay a visit to their land in
  mermaid form, Trot is enthusiastic, and Bill is too loyal to let her go off without him.

title: The School is on Fire!
author: Magdalena Cooper
description: One weekend, Teddy Bear, Ducky, and Fish go to the hill behind their school to roast some sweet potatoes. But suddenly, a strong wind comes and their fire spreads to the bushes. Soon, their school is on fire! What will the three friends do?

title: The Scarecrow of Oz
author: Lyman Frank Baum
description:
Cap'n Bill and Trot journey to Oz and, with the help of the Scarecrow, the former ruler of Oz, overthrow the villainous King Krewl of Jinxland. Cap'n Bill and Trot had
          previously appeared in two other novels by Baum, The Sea Fairies and Sky Island. Based in part upon the 1914 silent film, His Majesty, the Scarecrow of Oz. This was allegedly L. Frank
          Baum's personal favorite Oz book.

title: The Sausage Dog
author: Brenda Daniels
description: Thembsie really wants a dog, but she can’t have one. So Thembsie comes up with a plan of her own.

title: The Road to Oz
author: Lyman Frank Baum
description:
Meet Dorothy's new friends, the Shaggy Man, Button Bright and Polychrome, as you travel with them to the Emerald City. Share their adventures with the Musicker and the Scoodlers. See
  how they escape from the Soup-Kettle and what they found at the Truth Pond. Find out how they are able to cross the Deadly Desert and finally get to the Emerald City of Oz.

title: The River At Night
author: Nandini Majundar
description:
It is night and the author whimsically imagines that the river, the steps by the river and even the trees all go to sleep. Until the wind starts up and... A creative story line,
  almost as gentle as a soft lullaby being crooned in the night. This delightful book reminds me of the all-time classic Good Night Moon by Margaret Wise Brown in which a hush seems to envelop all
  around the little world of the child imparting a sense of peace, tanquillity and security. Adding to the charm of the book is the innovative use of zardoshi 'sewing with gold', for the font and the
  illustrations, a style of embroidery patronised by the mughal Emperors but now on a decline.

title: The Reluctant Dragon
author: Kenneth Grahame
description:
The Reluctant Dragon is an 1898 children's story by Kenneth Grahame (originally published as a chapter in his book Dream Days), which served as the key element to the 1941 feature
  film with the same name from Walt Disney Productions. The story has also been set to music as a children's operetta by John Rutter, with words by David Grant. The story takes place in the Berkshire
  Downs in Oxfordshire (where the author lived and where, according to legend, St George did fight a dragon). It is Grahame's most famous short story. It is arguably much more well-known than Dream
  Days itself or the related The Golden Age. It can be seen as a prototype to most modern stories in which the dragon is a sympathetic character rather than a threat.

title: The Red Raincoat
author: Kiran Kasturia
description: Manu has a new raincoat. He can't wait to wear it, but the rain makes him wait... and wait... and wait.

title: The Rainbow Fish
author: Jayashree Deshpande
description:
All of us enjoy watching fish, especially bright and colourful ones, swimming around in tanks that we keep in our homes. But do the fish enjoy it as much? Let's listen in on the
  conversation Raju and the rainbow fish have in this book, and find out.

title: The Race
author: A Mozambican folktale
description: Who will win if snail and rabbit have a race?

title: The Queen of Hearts
author: Randolph Caldecott
description:
Randolph Caldecott (1846-1886) was one of the most important British illustrators. He transformed the world of decorated children's books in the Victorian era. In 1877, he was asked
  by Edmund Evans, the colour printer and talented engraver, to illustrate two children's books. These books were an immediate success and he went on to produce two books every Christmas until he
  died. Caldecott chose all the stories and rhymes he illustrated and occasionally wrote and added to the stories himself. His delightful style and humour can still be enjoyed by young and old alike.
  This story, 'The Queen Of Hearts', was originally published in 1881. Many of the earliest children's books, particularly those dating back to the 1900s and before, are now extremely scarce and
  increasingly expensive. Pook Press are working to republish these classic works in affordable, high quality, colour editions, using the original text and artwork so these works can delight another
  generation of children

title: The Queen
author: Samira Saidani
description: Nectar, the queen bee, was sick of her life leading the swarm of bees. She decided to run away and never come back to her hive. Can she survive without her swarm?

title: The Princess of the School
author: Angela Brazil
description: On a certain morning, just a week before Christmas, the little world of school at Chilcombe Hall wasawake and stirring at an unusually early hour. Long before the slightest hint of dawn showed in thesky the lamps were lighted in the corridors, maids were scuttling about, bringing in breakfast, andJones, the gardener, assisted by his eldest boy, a sturdy grinning urchin of twelve, was beginning theprocess of carrying down piles of hand-bags and hold-alls, and stacking them on a cart which waswaiting in the drive outside.

title: The Princess and the Sunpati Flower
author: Binita Buddhacharya
keywords: The Princess and the Sunpati Flower
description: Each time a child is born to a king and queen, the queen’s younger sister secretly gives the child away to a fisherman. In despair, the king falls ill. A bird tells the king that only the sunpati flower can save his life. How will the king get the flower? Can he find his children?

title: The Princess and the Goblin
author: George Macdonald
description:
Eight-year-old Princess Irene lives a lonely life in a castle in a wild, desolate, mountainous kingdom, with only her nursemaid, Lootie for company. Her father the king is
          normally absent attending to affairs of state, and her mother is dead. Irene has never known about the existence of the goblins which lurk in the underground mines but her nursemaid Lootie
          does know about them.

title: The Prince who Smelled Smoky
author: Unknown
description:
This story has been produced for UNESCO as part of its commitment to the FRESH initiative (Focussing Resources on Effective School Health). The story deal with issues such as
  hygiene, sanitation, disease prevention, violence, discrimination and disaster preparedness. Story telling and story writing can not only confirm knowledge and raise interest but also develop a
  whole range of language and life skills and enhance vital attitudes which children need to develop at school.

title: The Portent and Other Stories
author: George Macdonald
publisher: Penn State Electronic Classic Series Publication

title: The Plant Whisperer
author: Sayantan Datta
description: Young Jaishree loves nothing more than plants. She wants to understand them, which is why she decides to spend her life studying plants. This biography of ecologist Dr H Jaishree Subrahmaniam is a story of passion and gumption.

title: The Pig With The Runaway Tail
author: Parinita Shetty
keywords: The Pig With The Runaway Tail
description: Pongal the pig has a bit of a problem. Her tail keeps running off on its own to have an adventure! Help Pongal find her runaway tail in this spotting book.

title: The Phoenix and the Carpet
author: Edith Nesbit
description:
It's startling enough to have a Phoenix hatch in your house, but even more startling when it reveals you have a magic carpet on the floor. Conceited it may be, but the
          Phoenix is also good-hearted, and obligingly accompanies the children on their adventures through time and space-which, magic being what it is, rarely turn out as they were
          meant...

title: The Peacoack 's Dance
author: Shahid Anwar
description: Hina went to the farm with her father one day. She saw a peacock dancing and started to dance as well. How did the peacock react? Read more to find out.

title: The Parrot with a Broken Beak
author: Shahid Anwar
keywords: The Parrot with a Broken Beak
description:
Her father's pen calls out to Kasni. Should she, or should she not pick it up? After she uses it, she uses it, she finds an angry father and an angry parrot. A tale with charming
  colours to make any child happy!

title: The Painted Jackal
author: Cbeebies
description:
This picture tale will help to develop your child’s language and literacy skills, as they listen to you read the text that appears on the screen. Reading this story with your
          child is a fun way of encouraging them to enjoy books and the whole process of storytelling, and is great for stimulating their imagination.

title: The Owl King's Night
author: Saktibrata Sen
description: Night falls and the owl king starts his gathering. Read more to find out about his night ahead!

title: The Orange Fairy Book
author: Andrew Lang
description:
Andrew Lang's Fairy Books — also known as Andrew Lang's "Coloured" Fairy Books or Andrew Lang's Fairy Books of Many Colors — are a series of twelve collections of fairy tales,
  published between 1889 and 1910.

title: The One and Only Human Body
author: Niranjana Sivaram
description: The human body is amazing! From the smallest muscle to the biggest organ—let’s explore how our bodies work.

title: The Old Couple and Selroti
author: Prabha Bhattarai
description: An old married couple is fighting. They both want more of a delicious, fried rice-flour doughnut called sel roti. But there are five sel roti. How will they decide who gets to eat three sel roti and who will eat two?

title: The Mythological Zoo
author: Oliver Herford
description:
Oliver Herford is adept at pairing whimsical illustrations with humorous poetry, and The Mythological Zoo is no exception. Each of the 22 illustrations of classic
          mythological beasts is accompanied by a brief poetic verse. Medusa, Cerberus, the Chimera, the Phoenix, and the Centaur grace these pages, amongst many more. These original drawings have
          been clarified and intensified from their original publication.

title: The Music Show
author: Hong Vannsothy
description: Goose wants to do a musical performance at the festival. Goose asks friends to join the band, but problems appear. Can they work together to make beautiful music?

title: The Mouse and the Pencil
author: V. Suteyev
description: A hilarious picture story of a mouse who found a pencil. Find out what mouse does with the pencil. Creatively illustrated picture book moves the story on.

title: The Mouse That Was
author: Paul Choy
description:
A picture book fable about a little mouse who learns about the significance of valuing what he has, over wanting what someone else has, and discovers that all he needed to be happy
  was himself.

title: The Mouse That Should
author: Paul Choy
description:
The Mouse That Should is the final part of Paul Choy's Little Mouse Trilogy. It is the story of a little mouse who learned that he should never leave for tomorrow, the things he
  could do today. Together, you and your children will discover how Little Mouse spends his summer days, in his little wood, and what happens once the winter arrives.

title: The Mouse That Knew
author: Paul Choy
description:
The mouse that knew, the second story from Paul Choy's modern fables series, is the story of a little mouse who knew that friends can achieve more together than they can by
  themselves. Together, you and your children will enjoy discovering how Little Mouse helps his friends in their quest for the juiciest apples in the wood.

title: The Milkmaid
author: Randolph Caldecott
description: “Where are you going, my Pretty Maid?”

title: The Memory Tree
author: Savnola Goldridge
description: Thembi and Thulani are sad. They miss Grandpa Nathi. Daddy and Mommy find a special way to remember Grandpa Nathi.

title: The Magical Glasses
author: Padmaparna Ghosh
description: Mirium and Tejas have magic glasses. Join them as they use the glasses to look at seven animals and birds that are found only in certain parts of the world.

title: The Magic of Oz
author: Lyman Frank Baum
description:
While searching for special birthday presents for Princess Ozma of Oz, Dorothy, the Wizard, and the Cowardly Lion discover a treasonous plot. In addition to familiar faces
          from previous Oz stories, this exciting and amusing tale introduces a host of new characters. 101 black-and-white drawings plus 12 full-color plates.

title: The Magic Soup
author: Janaki Sooriyarachchi
description: Vegetables, utensils and pots come together to make a magical and healthy soup for hungry Johney.

title: The Magic Mirror
author: Nin Monthakondeaklin
description: An evil witch curses the village, causing children to turn into scary creatures. Only Sam and Soy are free from the curse. Will Sam and Soy continue to escape the witch’s curse? Will the other children stay scary creatures forever?

title: The Lost Egg
author: Judie McEwan
description:
A wise old owl finds a lost egg, and wonders, whose egg it is. A few animals claim the egg to be theirs but the owl knows better. A beautifully illustrated story, with lots
          of interesting lessons.

title: The Lonely Whale Shark
author: Mahira Kakajiwala
description: A big little whale shark is sad and lonely on his reef. But when he meets a group of whale sharks, he realises all he needs to do is look around him.

title: The Little Red Hen
author: Florence White Williams
description: The story is a cautionary tale about how we reap what we sow. When the hen asks a duck, cat, and dog for help planting some wheat, she gets no takers. They won’t cut, thresh, or mill the wheat . . . or help bake bread with it, either. So guess who eats the bread by herself in the end?

title: The Little Old Woman who lived in a Shoe
author: Joseph Martin Kronheim
keywords: The Little Old Woman who lived in a Shoe

title: The Little Goat
author: Kaithong Mavongsa
readUrl: https://pustakalaya.org/media/uploads/documents/2022/08/16/ແບນອຍຂດ_eng_portrait_v120220811t1752470000_3fe72e1f/ແບນອຍຂດ_eng_PORTRAIT_V12022.08.11T1752470000.pdf
editor: Onchanh Phetchantharath,  Pakian Luangxaysana,  Sengmany Souphanthalop
description: A little goat likes to wander. One day he gets lost. How will he find the way back home?

title: The Little Girl on the Step
author: Unknown
description:
This story has been produced for UNESCO as part of its commitment to the FRESH initiative (Focussing Resources on Effective School Health). The story deal with issues such as
  hygiene, sanitation, disease prevention, violence, discrimination and disaster preparedness. Story telling and story writing can not only confirm knowledge and raise interest but also develop a
  whole range of language and life skills and enhance vital attitudes which children need to develop at school.

title: The Lion's Howdah
author: Amar Goswami
description: What happens when the king of the jungle imitates the king of the city? Many rocking adventures! Read this funny story to find out more.

title: The Lion Has Fever
author: Unknown
description:
This story has been produced for UNESCO as part of its commitment to the FRESH initiative (Focussing Resources on Effective School Health). The story deal with issues such as
  hygiene, sanitation, disease prevention, violence, discrimination and disaster preparedness. Story telling and story writing can not only confirm knowledge and raise interest but also develop a
  whole range of language and life skills and enhance vital attitudes which children need to develop at school.

title: The Lattice Window
author: Midesh Maharjan
description: The village of Kipu has a problem. A ghost is stealing children through the windows of their homes. Can the villagers come up with a plan to stop the ghost?

title: The Ladybird
author: Shantdas Manandhar
description: Two children discover a ladybird while walking back from school. What kind of insect is it?

title: The Lady or the Tiger
author: Frank Stockton
description:
Called the most famous riddle mystery of all time, this very short story poses a dilemma. A man is sentenced to an unusual punishment for having a romance with a king's
          beloved daughter. Taken to the public arena, he is faced with two doors, behind one of which is a hungry tiger that will devour him. Behind the other is a beautiful lady-in-waiting, whom he
          will have to marry if he finds her. While the crowd waits anxiously for his decision, he sees the princess among the spectators, who points him to the door on the right with a slight
          movement of her hand. The lover starts to open the door and ... Did the princess save her lover's life by pointing to the door leading to the lady-in-waiting, or did she prefer to see her
          lover die rather than see him marry someone else?

title: The Koel's Song
author: Jayashree Deshpande
description:
Why don't we ever hear the koel's sweet song in our cities anymore? City kid Raju finds out the answers to this and many other questions when he chats with a koel on his
  grandfather's farm.

title: The King's Crown
author: Richa Bhaskar
description: When King Anawrahta looked up to admire the tall pagoda, his crown fell down. Read this story set in present-day Myanmar to see if the crown stayed on his head.

title: The King of Root Valley And His Curious Daughter
author: Robert Reinick

title: The Killers' Committee
author: Unknown
description:
This story has been produced for UNESCO as part of its commitment to the FRESH initiative (Focussing Resources on Effective School Health). The story deal with issues such as
  hygiene, sanitation, disease prevention, violence, discrimination and disaster preparedness. Story telling and story writing can not only confirm knowledge and raise interest but also develop a
  whole range of language and life skills and enhance vital attitudes which children need to develop at school.

title: The Jungle School
author: Meera Tendolkar, Madhav Chavan
description: The animals in the jungle rush to the new school with great enthusiasm. What do you think happened after that?

title: The Invisible Poacher
author: Unknown
description:
This story has been produced for UNESCO as part of its commitment to the FRESH initiative (Focussing Resources on Effective School Health). The story deal with issues such as
  hygiene, sanitation, disease prevention, violence, discrimination and disaster preparedness. Story telling and story writing can not only confirm knowledge and raise interest but also develop a
  whole range of language and life skills and enhance vital attitudes which children need to develop at school.

title: The Innocence of Father Brown
author: Gilbert Keith Chesterton
description:
Father Brown is a fictional character created by English novelist G. K. Chesterton, who stars in 52 short stories, later compiled in five books. Chesterton based the character on
  Father John O’Connor (1870–1952), a parish priest in Bradford who was involved in Chesterton’s conversion to Catholicism in 1922. The relationship was recorded by O’Connor in his 1937 book Father
  Brown on Chesterton.

title: The Hunting of the Snark
author: Lewis Carroll
publisher: Penn State Electronic Classic Series Publication
description:
The nonsensical poem The Hunting of the Snark was written by Lewis Carroll in 1874 and published in 1876. Describing "with infinite humor the impossible voyage of an
          improbable crew to find an inconceivable creature", the work borrows in-part from Carroll's Jabberwocky in Through the Looking-Glass.

title: The House That Jack Built; A Game Of Forfeits.
author: Joana E. Dana

title: The House Of Arden: A Story For Children
author: E. Nesbit
description:
Orphaned Edred and Elfrida Arden live with their aunt, who keeps disagreeable lodgers for their livelihood. When the siblings take an illicit field trip to see the decaying Arden
  Castle, their family's ancestral home, they meet the Mouldiwarp, a magical white mole. Then the news comes that a distant relative has died, making Edred is Lord Arden and heir to the castle. They
  go to live there, although there is no money for its upkeep, and straightaway fall into magical adventures that take them journeying into history.

title: The History of Five Little Pigs
author: Joseph Martin Kronheim
keywords: The History of Five Little Pigs

title: The Hickory Ridge Boy Scouts
author: Captain Alan Douglas
keywords: Camp Fires of the Wolf Patrol

title: The Hare's Revenge
author: Unknown
description:
This story has been produced for UNESCO as part of its commitment to the FRESH initiative (Focussing Resources on Effective School Health). The story deal with issues such as
  hygiene, sanitation, disease prevention, violence, discrimination and disaster preparedness. Story telling and story writing can not only confirm knowledge and raise interest but also develop a
  whole range of language and life skills and enhance vital attitudes which children need to develop at school.

title: The Happy Lion
author: Louise Fatio
description:
This is the story of a happy lion who lived in a town zoo. The lion was happy because everybody who visited him were polite and he enjoyed their company. One day, as chance would
  have it, he got an opportunity to return their visits. And what do you think happened in the town when he went visiting! Contributed by: Arvind Gupta

title: The Greedy Mouse
author: Herminder Ohri
description: A mouse tries to carry a big bun home. Then he learns that it does not always pay to be greedy.

title: The Great Quest
author: Charles Boardman Hawes
description: A romance of 1826, wherein are recorded the experiences of Josiah Woods of Topham, and of those others with whom he sailed for Cuba and the Gulf of Guinea.

title: The Great Council of Fish
author: Shailesh Lal
description: The sea is in trouble. No one seems to have a solution. So it's time to gather the Great Council of Fish. Will the Council be able to save the sea?

title: The Goop Directory of Juvenile Offenders
author: Gelett Burgess
description: The Goop Directory of Juvenile Offenders Famous for their Misdeeds and Serving as a Salutary Example for all Virtuous Children

title: The Golden Key
author: George Macdonald
description: A woman tells her grandson of a golden key found at the end of a rainbow. One day, he sees a rainbow and sets out to find the end.

title: The Golden Balloon
author: Athanasia Gaitanidou
description:
But I’m a balloon just like you, it said hesitantly to the round balloons that were looking from up high and were laughing at it. It was different from the rest, with a rare,
          almost gold colour. It had every right to be proud of its appearance but it had yet to realise how beautiful and special it was. All of this though, up to the point that…

title: The Girl Who Could Not Stop Laughing
author: Meera Ganapathi
description: Every day T. Sundari gets into trouble because most things make her laugh. She just cannot keep her mouth sealed. T. Sundari wants to know if something is wrong with her. Because if there isn't, she can laugh all the time!

title: The Giant and the Ants
author: Johnny Wheeler
description: A mighty giant gets his comeuppance in this original tale by Johnny Wheeler.

title: The Generous Crow
author: Venkatramana Gowda
description:
The crow is not beautiful. She can neither sing as sweetly as a cuckoo nor dance as gracefully as a peacock. But she has one unique quality that we can all learn from. Read the book
  to find out what it is!

title: The Fox jumps over the Parson’s Gate
author: Randolf Caldecott

title: The Fox Jumps Over the Parson's Gate
author: Randolph Caldecott
description:
One of a series of classic Victorian children's books by the British artist and author. Caldecott was the eponym of the Caldecott Medal and transformed the world of children's books
  in the Victorian era. He exercised his art chiefly in book illustrations, which were full of life, and instinct with a kindly, graceful humour. The stories and rhymes were all of his choosing and
  in some cases were written or added to by himself.

title: The Fountain
author: Aparna Kshirsagar
description: The street outside Ramesh’s house is all dug up. Ramesh finds a water pipe peeping out of the mud. And then…such fun!

title: The Fairy Tale Trap
author: Emily Casey
description:
Ivy has never liked mirrors. So of course, without warning, one of them sucks her into the fairy tale Beauty and the Beast. When Ivy tries to escape her fairy tale prison, she breaks
  the wrong spell. Now Beast is not so gentle-on-the-inside and Beauty is falling for the wrong prince. Perfect. Magic mirrors? Flushing chamber pots? Ivy is so there. Can she escape the fairy tale
  trap?

title: The Evil Forest
author: Joseph Sanchez Nadimo
description: Three sisters go to the forest in search of firewood, but only two of them return home. What happens to the third sister.

title: The Emerald City of Oz
author: Lyman Frank Baum
description:
The Emerald City is built all of beautiful marbles in which are set a profusion of emeralds, every one exquisitely cut and of very great size. There are other jewels used in the
  decorations inside the houses and palaces, such as rubies, diamonds, sapphires, amethysts and turquoises. But in the streets and upon the outside of the buildings only emeralds appear, from which
  circumstance the place is named the Emerald City of Oz.

title: The Elephant's Child
author: Rudyard Kipling
description:
The Elephant’s Child by Rudyard Kipling; Illustrations by Jean Pierre Petit Taken from the “Just So stories” for little children, this is a highly fantasised ‘origin story’ that
  speaks of how the elephant got its long trunk.

title: The Elephant Bird
author: Arefa Tehsin
description:
Munia knew that the giant one-feathered elephant bird had not swallowed the horse, even though he was big enough to swallow one! So where had the horse disappeared? A story about a
  magical bird, and a brave and curious child.

title: The Doll That Bommakka Made
author: Sheela Preuitt, Praba Ram
description: This charming cumulative tale celebrates the tradition of hand-crafted dolls, inspired by the South Indian Thanjavur Thalai Atti Bommai. Starting with a little ball of clay, we see the fine dancing doll grow before our eyes. The rhythmic descriptive words, stacked in a delightfully repetitive way, invite children to chant along. The vibrant illustrations complete the vivid imagery.

title: The Dog Who Knew Sadness
author: Nisarg Prakash
description: Sadness follows Feroz like a shadow. But his best friend Noah is always there to chase it away.

title: The Dividing Lines
author: Kapil Pandey ‘Kislay’
description: A poet wakes up to a wonderful dream, one that imagines a world without borders.

title: The Day the Earth Shook
author: Unknown
description:
This story has been produced for UNESCO as part of its commitment to the FRESH initiative (Focussing Resources on Effective School Health). The story deal with issues such as
  hygiene, sanitation, disease prevention, violence, discrimination and disaster preparedness. Story telling and story writing can not only confirm knowledge and raise interest but also develop a
  whole range of language and life skills and enhance vital attitudes which children need to develop at school.

title: The Day It Rained Fish
author: Ramendra Kumar
description:
In a canopy forest in India, the Up World and Down World have always been suspicious of each other. But it all changes when Gopa the dormouse drops her book by accident of Fatima's
  head. A story about friendship and the biodiversity of canopy forest.

title: The Crying Guitar
author: Rania Kyrkintanou
description:
The strongest desire a guitar can have is to play music. However, this is not so easy for a defective guitar. She starts her adventure in a musical instrument store, she goes for a
  while at the conservatory, she meets a damaged stove, an old refrigerator and other strange objects, and finally she ends up in a dumpster. Everything shows that she has the same destiny as the
  garbage. Or not?

title: The Crimson Fairy Book
author: Andrew Lang
description: A collection of fairy tales.

title: The Clown's Life
author: Alkmini Giampanidou
description:
When a young boy's dream is to make the whole world happy, there is no choice left but to become a… CLOWN! His love for young children leads him to play for the rest of his life the
  nicest role! He disguises himself and with his tricks he gives his friends laughter and LOVE.

title: The Clever Tortoise
author: Prashaanth Ramalingam
description: The tortoise sees the monkeys eating wood apples and wants to taste them. But first, he has to figure out how to crack open the hard shell. Can you help him?

title: The Children's Object Book
author: F. Warne & Co.
description: A picture book featuring everyday people, places and things.

title: The Cat in the Ghat
author: Ambika Rao
description:
This is a book that takes you deep into the jungles of the Western Ghats. A wildlife photographer sets out to find an elusive wild cat and meets a menagerie of fascinating creatures.
  Quirky illustrations pepper a funny narrative inspired by a real-life adventure. What better way to invite you to join his quest!

title: The Burgess Bird Book for Children
author: Thornton W. Burgess
keywords: The Burgess Bird Book for Children

title: The Burgess Animal Book for Children
author: Thornton W. Burgess
keywords: The Burgess Animal Book for Children

title: The Bubble Mystery
author: Murari Jha
description: Toot-Toot is afraid of the water until she notices some funny bubbles. When she finally bathes in the pond, she sees lots of bubbles that go blop, blop, blop! Where do they come from? No one will answer when she asks. Can Toot-Toot solve the bubble mystery?

title: The Boy and the Drum
author: Umesh P N
description:
A folktale about giving and kindness transforms into a lively play! This versatile and adaptable piece can be performed on stage or in the classroom. Hours of fun and learning
  guaranteed!

title: The Box
author: Tania Kliphuis
description: Dad comes home with a box. Boring. Until Max and Andi’s friends come to play… What will they do with the box?

title: The Box
author: Marina Apostolou
description:
“We need each other”… what a cliché phrase, mentioned thousands of times but inapplicable. Are we really informed about transplantations in Greece? How tragic is the truth on that
  specific issue in our country? Demonization, taboo, hesitation till the “evil” knocks on our door and then we realize how much ignorance and absence of mutual understanding hurt. Greece, year 2012.
  Endless waiting lists for a transplant. A mentality that doesn’t change. But what happens in the end and what is the price we must pay for our narrow minds?

title: The Boat Ride
author: Herminder Ohri
description: Vikki, the squirrel likes to talk big. His cousin came to visit him and they went on a boat ride. They were having fun when things turned rather adventurous...

title: The Blue Fairy Book
author: Andrew Lang
description:
Andrew Lang's Fairy Books or Andrew Lang's "Coloured" Fairy Books constitute a twelve-book series of fairy tale collections. Although Andrew Lang did not collect the stories
          himself from the oral tradition, the extent of his sources, who had collected them originally (with the notable exception of Madame d'Aulnoy), made them an immensely influential collection,
          especially as he used foreign-language sources, giving many of these tales their first appearance in English. As acknowledged in the prefaces, although Lang himself made most of the
          selections, his wife and other translators did a large portion of the translating and telling of the actual stories. The Blue Fairy Book assembled a wide range of tales, with seven from the
          Brothers Grimm, five from Madame d'Aulnoy, three from the Arabian Nights, and four Norse stories, among other sources. (wikipedia)

title: The Blue Fairy
author: Zahid Rahman, Uttam Kumar Dhar
description: The Blue Fairy is a tale about two young girls who befriend a fairy and play with her.

title: The Best Nest
author: Crystal Warren
description: Two birds go on a quest to find the best nest ever.

title: The Best Christmas Gift
author: Ivan Parvov
description:
Another adventure with the small for Bubu. This time, it's Christmas, and Lulu helps Santa with an important task. Beautiful illustrations, and a sweet story, with a nice moral to
  help children learn about values and rules.

title: The Bee and the Elephant
author: Long Ravy
description: An elephant tries to help a little lost bee find his home. Is it the nest? The cave? Where does he live?
